
# Align-fastqs test fixtures
These fixtures are synthetic micro-fixtures for fast, deterministic tests of the align-fastqs workflow.

They are intentionally small and hand-checkable. Running `make.sh` from `env_protocol` regenerates the fixture set deterministically.

Regenerate fixtures from the repository root with:
```bash
source activate env_protocol
bash tests/fixtures/align_fastqs/make.sh
```

Generated fixture outputs are ignored by Git. When required inputs are missing, `tests/run_tests.sh` regenerates this fixture set automatically.

The fixture set focuses on single-end and paired-end Bowtie 2 alignment to BAM and CRAM output, plus BWA MEM, BWA ALN, and bwa-mem2 MEM alignment to BAM output. These fixtures are not derived from real sequencing data. The reference sequence and FASTQ records are encoded directly in `make.sh` so that the expected read alignments are easy to inspect.

<br />

## Expected alignment behavior
The single-end FASTQ fixture contains one read:

| Read name        | Sequence                         | Expected reference |
| :---             | :---                             | :---               |
| `tiny_se_read_1` | `ACGTTGACCGTTAACGATCGTAGCTAGGAT` | `I`                |

Bowtie 2, BWA MEM, BWA ALN, and bwa-mem2 MEM should align this read to chromosome `I` in the tiny reference. Tests should verify that wrapper-generated BAM/CRAM files and indexes exist, pass `samtools quickcheck`, report or count one read alignment on `I`, and contain the expected read name. CRAM checks should read with `samtools view -T reference/tiny.fa`.

The paired-end FASTQ fixtures contain one read pair:

| Read name        | Mate | Sequence                         | Expected reference | Expected start |
| :---             | :--- | :---                             | :---               | :---           |
| `tiny_pe_pair_1` | R1   | `ACGTTGACCGTTAACGATCGTAGCTAGGAT` | `I`                | 17             |
| `tiny_pe_pair_1` | R2   | `CCTTAGCCGATTAGCCTAAGCTTGATCCGG` | `I`                | 70             |

R1 matches chromosome `I` in forward orientation. R2 is the reverse complement of positions 70-99 on chromosome `I`, so Bowtie 2, BWA MEM, BWA ALN, and bwa-mem2 MEM should report the pair in FR orientation. Tests should verify that wrapper-generated BAM/CRAM files and indexes exist, pass `samtools quickcheck`, report or count two read alignments on `I`, contain the expected paired read name, and include proper-pair flag records when the aligner reports stable proper-pair flags. CRAM checks should read with `samtools view -T reference/tiny.fa`.

<br />

### Repeat fixtures
`make.sh` writes one 150-base repeat and four 400-base unique blocks literally, then joins them into the 2,050-base reference `chrR`: the unique blocks separated by three copies of the repeat. A read wholly in the repeat therefore has three equally good placements. The 100-base reads are cut from the blocks:

| Read name | R1                                            | R2     | In single-end input |
| :---      | :---                                          | :---   | :---                |
| `chim`    | 60 bases of repeat, then 40 of unique block 3 | unique | yes                 |
| `rchm`    | 60 bases of unique block 3, then 40 of repeat | unique | yes                 |
| `half`    | wholly in the repeat                          | unique | no                  |
| `ctrl`    | unique                                        | unique | yes                 |

With BWA MEM and bwa-mem2, `chim` R1 is a split read with its primary in the repeat, `rchm` R1 a split read with its supplementary in the repeat, and `half` a pair whose mates get different MAPQ; BWA ALN gives `half` different mate MAPQs too. Bowtie 2 writes no supplementary records. `test_align_fastqs_mapq_template.sh` checks the MAPQs each aligner writes before relying on them.

The queryname-copy reads are three 50-base pairs from 300-base fragments of `chrR`, at zero-based offsets 50 (`uniq`) and 1,200 (`dup_a` and `dup_b`, one fragment under two names, so duplicate marking marks one of them). R1 starts the fragment on the forward strand, and R2 is the reverse complement of its last 50 bases.

In the SAM fixtures, template `sec_keep` has primary records at MAPQ 60 and a secondary record at MAPQ 0, and `sec_drop` has a primary record at MAPQ 0 and a secondary record at MAPQ 255. Filtered at MAPQ 30 by primary records, only `sec_keep` is kept, with its secondary record. Template `unal_mate` has an aligned R1 and an R2 flagged unaligned (0x4) whose partner lacks 0x8, the shape `bwa sampe` writes in #75, and the single-end file holds an unaligned read, `unal`. Both unaligned records keep MAPQ 60, so the filter must drop them by their flag, not their MAPQ.

<br />

### Tie fixtures
`make.sh` runs `make_tie.py`, which draws the tie reference and reads through `random.Random(0).random()`. Python guarantees that stream across versions, so the data are random in content but identical on every run and every host. The reference has two chromosomes, `chrT1` and `chrT2`. Each holds three 3,000-base unique blocks, each followed by a copy of one shared 600-base repeat, and ends with a 1,000-base unique block. A read inside a repeat copy has six equally good placements, and Bowtie 2 picks one with a per-read random generator. The reads are 1,000 pairs of 50-base mates cut from 150- to 400-base fragments on either strand. About 30% of mates carry one mismatch.

The same reads come under three header forms. Bowtie 2 seeds each read's generator from its sequence, its qualities, its whole FASTQ header line, and `--seed`. For a pair, it combines the two mates' seeds by exclusive or, which cancels every term the mates share:

| Files     | R1 header                | R2 header                | Change from the row above |
| :---      | :---                     | :---                     | :---                      |
| `tie_pe`  | `tie_<n>`                | `tie_<n>`                |                           |
| `tie_cmt` | `tie_<n> 1:N:0:AAAAAAAA` | `tie_<n> 2:N:0:AAAAAAAA` | the mates now differ      |
| `tie_idx` | `tie_<n> 1:N:0:CCCCCCCC` | `tie_<n> 2:N:0:CCCCCCCC` | a change both mates share |

The single-end files `tie_se` and `tie_cmt_se` hold the R1 reads with the `tie_pe` and `tie_cmt` headers.

Measured with Bowtie 2 2.5.5 and the pipeline's default paired-end call, about 164 of the 2,000 paired-end records and 144 of the 1,000 single-end records are tied (MAPQ 0 or 1). A record moves when its flag, reference, position, MAPQ, CIGAR, or mate fields change. From `tie_pe` to `tie_cmt`, about 136 paired-end records move; from `tie_cmt` to `tie_idx`, none do; changing `--seed` moves no paired-end record but about 123 single-end ones; and `--seed 0` gives the same output as no `--seed`. With `-p 8`, the output order differs from `-p 1` while the records do not, and `--reorder` restores the `-p 1` order. With BWA-MEM (0.7.19) and BWA-MEM2 (2.3), changing `-K 100000000` to `-K 10000` moves 2 paired-end records because insert sizes are estimated per batch. The whole set is smaller than one default batch, so the thread count alone moves none.

<br />

### Bridge fixtures
`make.sh` joins the repeat fixtures' unique blocks into two contigs: `chrA` (blocks 0 and 1, 800 bases) and `chrB` (blocks 2 and 3, 800 bases). The 100-base pairs are cut from them:

| Read name | R1                       | R2                                                                           |
| :---      | :---                     | :---                                                                         |
| `brdg`    | unique in `chrA`, at 501 | reverse complement of the last 70 bases of `chrA` and the first 30 of `chrB` |
| `ctrl`    | unique in `chrB`         | unique in `chrB`                                                             |

With BWA ALN (0.7.19), `bwa sampe` flags `brdg` R2 unaligned (0x4) but keeps its position. It leaves R1's mate-unaligned flag (0x8) clear, so a per-record `samtools view -F 12` keeps R1 alone. BWA MEM and bwa-mem2 MEM align R2 in part and write a supplementary record on `chrB`. Bowtie 2 end-to-end leaves R2 unaligned and flags R1's mate unaligned. Bowtie 2 local aligns R2 in part. `test_align_fastqs_unaligned.sh` checks the raw BWA ALN flags before relying on them.

<br />

### Pairs fixtures
`make.sh` runs `make_pairs.py`, which draws the pairs reference and reads through `random.Random(0).random()`, as `make_tie.py` does. The reference has two chromosomes of random unique sequence. `chrP1` is 6,000 bases, with copies of one 300-base repeat at zero-based offsets 1,000, 2,500, and 4,000. `chrP2` is 3,000 bases. Each 50-base pair belongs to one class (offsets are zero-based leftmost positions of each mate's alignment):

| Read name    | R1                    | R2                             | Class                         |
| :---         | :---                  | :---                           | :---                          |
| `pair_conc`  | forward, `chrP1` 100  | reverse, `chrP1` 350           | concordant, 300-base fragment |
| `pair_ovlp`  | forward, `chrP1` 500  | reverse, `chrP1` 520           | mates overlap                 |
| `pair_cont`  | forward, `chrP1` 700  | reverse, 30 bases, `chrP1` 720 | R2 contained in R1            |
| `pair_far`   | forward, `chrP1` 4400 | reverse, `chrP1` 5850          | 1,500-base fragment           |
| `pair_dove`  | forward, `chrP1` 1500 | reverse, `chrP1` 1490          | dovetailed                    |
| `pair_rf`    | reverse, `chrP1` 1700 | forward, `chrP1` 1950          | outward-facing (RF)           |
| `pair_ff`    | forward, `chrP1` 2000 | forward, `chrP1` 2200          | same strand (FF)              |
| `pair_chrs`  | forward, `chrP1` 3000 | reverse, `chrP2` 500           | different chromosomes         |
| `pair_one`   | forward, `chrP1` 3300 | random                         | one mate unaligned            |
| `pair_none`  | random                | random                         | both mates unaligned          |
| `pair_rpt`   | forward, `chrP1` 2550 | reverse, `chrP1` 2850          | R1 in the repeat              |
| `pair_conc2` | forward, `chrP2` 1000 | reverse, `chrP2` 1200          | concordant                    |

With Bowtie 2 2.5.5's default paired-end call (`--no-mixed --no-discordant -X 1000`), the concordant, overlapping, contained, and repeat pairs align concordantly (mate rescue places `pair_rpt`), and every other pair is written with both mates unaligned (flags 77 and 141). With the relaxed call (`-I 0 -X 1000`), `pair_far`, `pair_dove`, and `pair_chrs` are discordant, `pair_rf` and `pair_ff` keep their orientations, and `pair_one` has its R1 aligned (73 and 133). BWA MEM (0.7.19) cannot estimate insert sizes from so few pairs, so it flags no pair as proper; it aligns every mate the relaxed call does. `test_align_fastqs_unal_mode.sh` checks the side file's read names per call against these.

The filled set holds the twelve pair classes, under the same names, and 300 concordant filler pairs (`fill_000` to `fill_299`) in the unique blocks, away from the repeat copies, with fragments of 200 to 300 bases. Each filler pair starts at its own position, so none is a duplicate. `make_pairs.py` draws nothing at random for this set, so the other sets are unchanged. With the fillers, BWA MEM and bwa-mem2 MEM estimate insert sizes and flag pairs proper: every filler pair and `pair_conc`, `pair_ovlp`, `pair_cont`, `pair_rpt`, and `pair_conc2` (99 and 147), but not `pair_far`, `pair_dove`, `pair_chrs` (97 and 145), `pair_rf` (81 and 161), or `pair_ff` (65 and 129); `pair_one` (73 and 133) and `pair_none` (77 and 141) are as in the pairs set. `test_align_fastqs_unal_mode.sh` checks that BWA flags at least 600 records proper before relying on them.

The single-end file holds `se_uniq` (forward, `chrP1` 200), `se_uniq2` (reverse, `chrP2` 2000), `se_rpt` (in the repeat), and `se_none` (random).

The duplicate set's names carry flow-cell coordinates (`A00123:8:HFLOWCELL:1:1101:<x>:<y>`). Its first pair is concordant on `chrP2` (R1 at 1500, x and y 1000). The other five have a random, unaligned R2, and their R1 is aligned: one at the first pair's R1 (x and y 20000); two at 2200, far apart on the tile; and two at 2600, 100 pixels apart in x and y. With BWA MEM and `--unal_mode separate`, `samtools markdup` marks the first of these as a duplicate of the pair's R1, one of the two at 2200 as a library duplicate, and one of the two at 2600 as an optical duplicate.

In `sam/split_template_pe.sam`, `t75` has an aligned R1 and an R2 flagged unaligned (0x4) whose partner lacks 0x8, as `bwa sampe` writes (#75); `supp` is the same with a supplementary record for R1; `pair` is a complete pair; `lone` is an aligned R1 with no R2 record; and `ffpp` is a same-strand pair flagged proper, which `samtools fixmate` unflags, so `-f 2` keeps it only before `fixmate`.

<br />

## Current and deferred test coverage
The test suite covers submit- and execute-layer single-end and paired-end alignment, a local Bowtie 2 GNU Parallel path gated by `RUN_PARALLEL=1`, and a remote Slurm submission path gated by `RUN_SLURM=1`. Set `WAIT_SLURM=1` with `RUN_SLURM=1` to poll for expected Slurm outputs.
